text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: CRIT: GPU node pool 'inference-prod-pool' at 100% utilization; autoscaler unable to add nodes — reached configured max_nodes limit (48). Queue length rising. Paging on-call.

maya.c: saw the pager, jumping in. what's the current queue depth / p95 tail?

sam_o: queue depth ~11.8k, front-end is returning 429s for a subset of requests. p95 latency for generate endpoint 1.8s -> 7.4s over last 10m. customer-facing errors spiking.

alex: thanks. any recent deploys or config changes to HPA/cluster-autoscaler?

sam_o: no deploys to serving runtime in the last 2 hours. autoscaler logs show: `failed to scale: at max nodes` and `scale attempt blocked by cloud-provider quota: maxInstancesReached`.

maya.c: grabbing current node counts and pod evictions.

maya.c: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-prod-pool -o wide | wc -l` -> 48

maya.c: `kubectl top nodes | sort -k3 -nr | head -n5` shows all GPUs ~98-100% memory and GPU utilization.

katp: customer-support-bot reporting: some large batch jobs being queued, several enterprise customers seeing timeouts. severity S2 for now, potential S1 if degradation continues.

alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) manual bump max_nodes on the pool to allow autoscaler to add nodes; 2) temporarily enable burst capacity to a smaller cheaper GPU SKU (if available); 3) enable request throttling/rate limit at LB to protect control plane; 4) evict low-priority jobs / preemptible pods.

maya.c: can we do (1) quickly? who's got permissions to update the pool? I don't have cloud-project-owner.

sam_o: I can request a manual increase, but it's a console action that requires infra-admin approval for the org project. I'll open a manual cap raise request and ping infra-admins.

sam_o: @alex @katp opening ticket: "Request: temporary increase inference-prod-pool max_nodes to 64 for 2h". tagging infra-admins.

support-bot: customer-impact summary: ~3 customers experiencing 45-60s timeouts, ~1200 requests failed in last 5m. Escalating to account managers for top 5 customers.

alex: while we wait for infra-admins, can we reduce queue pressure: - disable heavy batch slots by label; - pause non-critical canaries; - divert traffic to fallback smaller model variant for non-enterprise tokens.

maya.c: patch coming: I'll annotate the canary deployments to scale-to-zero. `kubectl patch deployment batch-worker -n inference --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'`

maya.c: done. taking down batch-workers; queue dropped ~1.2k in 2m. now 10.6k. p95 down to 6.1s.

sam_o: infra-admin @chris has accepted the manual cap raise. performing increase now.

deploy-bot: Running cloud CLI: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling ... --max-num-replicas 64` (redacted)

sam_o: cloud confirm: new max_nodes applied, autoscaler triggered provisioning of 8 additional instances. ETA ~4-7m for nodes to be ready.

maya.c: adding temporary routing rule to direct non-enterprise traffic to model-compact to reduce token spend.

maya.c: `curl -s https://internal-router/route -X POST -d '{"route":"model-compact","match":"non-enterprise"}'` -> 200 OK.

katp: notifying customer success + posting status update to customer incident channel.

support-bot: posted customer update: "We're experiencing degraded throughput due to capacity limits; temporary routing and scaling changes applied; engineering is on it. ETA 10-15m."

alex: monitoring node join logs. once nodes join we'll watch pod scheduling and warm-up (KV cache). expect some latency as new nodes start.

maya.c: new nodes are registering: `kubectl get nodes | tail -n8` shows 6 new nodes Ready. GPU pools now 54 total.

sam_o: autoscaler now scheduling pods onto new nodes. queue draining rate increasing. p95 trending down to 2.2s. 429s dropping.

alex: action items for next hour: - revert batch-worker scale-to-zero only after queue <500 and stable for 10m (maya) - follow up with infra on increasing pool default max_nodes and alerting (sam) - create a post-incident MOP to avoid manual console steps (alex)

maya.c: agreed. I'll keep watch and coordinate handoff in 30m.

katp: logging postmortem stub and paging summary in #postmortems. tagging customer CS notes.

support-bot: final customer update posted: "Capacity increased and routing changes applied; performance recovering. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

alex: handing off to evening oncall @sam_o in 30m. if anything regresses escalate to infra-admins again.

sam_o: acknowledged. creating follow-up ticket for quota / policy changes: "Autoscaler ceiling triggered — propose increasing soft limits and automating emergency cap raise via runbook".

maya.c: thanks team. leaving monitoring channel open. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Autoscaler ceiling lifted via manual cap increase; queue recovered. Summary written to #postmortems/1729500000."
